title: Rotate SDDC Manager 9.0 credentials without stranding in-flight requests on the old secret
prompt:
Implement `credrotate/rotate.go` as a standard-library-only Go package that rotates resource credentials held by a VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 SDDC Manager appliance. Do not add dependencies and do not edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection taken directly from `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, immutable commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`. `docs/official_sources.json` repeats that provenance and records the spec path, the commit sha, every operationId and the JSON pointer each projected claim was read from. No rendered documentation page is a contract source, and the 9.1.0.0 revision of the same file (commit `3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26`) is not the contract: among the schemas this contract projects it widens `ResourceCredentials.resourceType` from `ESXI, VCENTER, PSC, NSXT_MANAGER, NSXT_EDGE, NSX_ALB, BACKUP` to additionally include `HCX_MANAGER` and `VSP`. Use exactly the specification operationIds `updateOrRotatePasswords`, `getCredentialsTask` and `cancelCredentialsTask`; do not call any other route.

Preserve the supplied public API: `NewStore(secrets map[Key]Secret) (*Store, error)`, `(*Store).Acquire(ctx context.Context, key Key) (Secret, func(), error)`, `(*Store).Snapshot() map[Key]Secret`, `NewClient(baseURL, accessToken string, httpClient *http.Client) (*Client, error)`, `(*Client).Rotate(ctx context.Context, store *Store, req RotateRequest, pollInterval time.Duration) (Result, error)`, and the supplied `Key`, `Secret`, `CredentialSpec`, `ResourceSpec`, `AutoRotatePolicy`, `RotateRequest`, `Outcome`, `Result`, `APIError` and `RotationFailedError` types. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Reject an empty or non-HTTP(S) service-root URL and a blank or header-unsafe access token. Never place an access token or a password in an error, and never put a password in a `Result`.

Rotation is destructive and asynchronous: once the appliance starts changing a password the old secret stops working, so a caller still using it is stranded. Callers borrow a secret with `Acquire` and hand it back through the release function it returns; releasing twice is harmless. `Rotate` must seal every credential it is about to change so no new borrower is handed a secret that is about to be retired, wait until every already-borrowed one has been handed back, and only then send `updateOrRotatePasswords`. Nothing may reach the appliance before that drain finishes. Context cancellation or deadline expiry must stop the wait and the polling promptly, and the returned error must wrap `ctx.Err()`. However the rotation ends, including when it is abandoned, the seal must be lifted, or every later borrower waits forever. A `Store` is safe for concurrent use, and `Acquire` blocks a borrower that arrives mid-rotation until that rotation settles, then hands it whichever secret is live afterwards.

`updateOrRotatePasswords` is `PATCH /v1/credentials` with exact success status 202. Its accepted representation is a `Task`, not a `CredentialsTask`: validate the `Task`'s required `id`, `name`, `status` and `creationTimestamp`, and take its nonblank `id`. The `Task` status vocabulary carries mixed-case spellings such as `Pending` and `In Progress`, so normalize any status by trimming it, uppercasing it, then replacing each run of whitespace with a single underscore. Because the accepted `Task` carries no subtasks, call `getCredentialsTask` for that exact id at least once even when the accepted status already looks terminal. `getCredentialsTask` is a bodyless `GET /v1/credentials/tasks/{id}` with exact success status 200, and every polled id must match the accepted id. Its `CredentialsTask` status vocabulary is the one that decides the outcome: `PENDING` and `IN_PROGRESS` are nonterminal and must be polled again after `pollInterval`; `SUCCESSFUL` is success; `FAILED`, `USER_CANCELLED` and `INCONSISTENT` are unsuccessful terminal states; any other status is a contract violation rather than a reason to keep polling. A credentials task that settled `FAILED` or `INCONSISTENT` stays on the appliance and blocks the next one, so retire it with `cancelCredentialsTask`, a bodyless `DELETE /v1/credentials/tasks/{id}` with exact success status 202, before reporting. Do not cancel a task that settled `SUCCESSFUL` or `USER_CANCELLED`.

A rotation can settle partially, so which secret is now live is decided per credential from the settled task's `subTasks`, never from the overall status. A subtask correlates to a credential by its `resourceName` and `username`, not by a resource id; a subtask that names neither is orchestration and a subtask for a credential this change did not touch is not yours, and both are skipped. `Result.Outcomes` holds one entry per correlated subtask in subtask order, with the normalized subtask status. A credential moved to a new secret only when its subtask is `SUCCESSFUL` and carries a nonblank `newPassword`; the appliance may report a `newPassword` on a subtask that failed, and that candidate never became live. Publish exactly the credentials that moved, incrementing each one's `Generation`, and do so before the seal is lifted, so no borrower can be handed a retired secret and none is left on an old secret the appliance has already replaced. For a credential that did not move, `ErrorCode` and `Message` come from its subtask's first error.

`Rotate` always returns a populated `Result`, including alongside a non-nil error. `TaskID` and `TaskStatus` are set as soon as they are known, `TaskStatus` being the normalized status last observed or the normalized accepted-`Task` status when polling never produced one. `Succeeded` is true only when the credentials task settled `SUCCESSFUL`, and `Cancelled` reports whether `cancelCredentialsTask` was issued. `Rotated` and `Retained` partition the sealed credentials in request order into those that moved and those that kept the secret they had; when nothing was changed, every credential is retained. A non-success HTTP status is an `*APIError` carrying the operationId, the status code, and the `errorCode` and `message` from the response's `Error` body. A credentials task that settles in an unsuccessful terminal state is a `*RotationFailedError` carrying the task id, the normalized status, the task's first `errorCode` and `message`, and the per-credential outcomes; the HTTP calls all succeeded in that case, and the change still did not.

Refuse a bad change before anything reaches the appliance and before any credential is sealed: an `operationType` outside the pinned vocabulary, a `resourceType` outside the 9.0.0.0 vocabulary including the two values that exist only in the 9.1.0.0 revision, a missing resource name, a resource with no credentials, a credential with no username, the same credential twice, a credential the store does not hold, an `UPDATE` whose credential supplies no password, a non-`UPDATE` that supplies a password the appliance generates itself, a nil store, and a nonpositive poll interval.

Honor the exact wire contract. Send only writable members: a readOnly member of `Task`, `CredentialsTask` or `CredentialsSubTask` is never present in a request. An unset optional member is absent from the encoded JSON rather than encoded as null, an empty string, zero or any other placeholder, and omission is decided per array element, so one `ResourceCredentials` element may carry `resourceId` while its sibling omits it and one `BaseCredential` element may carry `accountType` while its sibling omits it. A required member is still sent when it holds a zero value: `AutoRotateCredentialPolicyInputSpec.enableAutoRotatePolicy` is required, so `false` travels as `false`, while the optional `frequencyInDays` beside it is omitted when it is zero. The whole `autoRotatePolicy` member is absent when no policy is supplied. Every request carries exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` and one `Accept: application/json`; the one request with a body carries exactly one `Content-Type: application/json`, while `getCredentialsTask` and `cancelCredentialsTask` send no body and therefore no `Content-Type`. The task id is percent-escaped as a single path segment, and no request carries a query string or a bare `?`.

Run `go test -race ./...`. The protected, table-driven verifier sends genuine HTTP requests through the shipped contract-pinned mock, using an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` listener when sockets are available and the same handler through an in-process transport otherwise, and reads its mutex-guarded request log. The mock loads its only three callable routes from `docs/contract.json` and refuses anything else, along with any request whose headers, target or body shape departs from that contract. Verification drives the rotation to full success, to a partial settlement that leaves two credentials on new secrets and one on its old one, to a refusal of the change itself and to a failure while polling; it holds a borrowed secret across a rotation and runs concurrent borrowers against it; and it asserts the served operation sequence, the exact request targets and header multiplicity, and the exact member set of every request body. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `docs/`, `internal/` and `go.mod` are protected fixtures and must not be changed.

commands.name: race-tests
cmd: task_cache=$(mktemp -d) && trap 'find "$task_cache" -depth -delete' EXIT && GOCACHE="$task_cache/go-build" CCACHE_DISABLE=1 go test -race -count=1 -timeout 60s ./...
